# Create New Issue
<!-- DO NOT EDIT this file directly. It is maintained by fhc sync and will be overwritten.
     Source: templates/skills/new-issue/SKILL.md in fh-commons -->

Create a new Forgejo issue following the standard workflow.

## CRITICAL: Tool Constraints

**This repository uses Forgejo (NOT GitHub)**
- **ALWAYS use:** `flu git` commands
- **NEVER use:** `gh` or `tea` commands

> **Issue Backend:** All `flu issue` commands accept `--backend BACKEND`
> (`forgejo` | `psql`; default: `forgejo`). Projects using the psql backend
> (e.g. PAT) should pass `--backend psql` or set `issue.backend_default`
> in `.fhc-config.json`. Note: `bulk`, `move`, and `report` subcommands
> do not yet support psql (see #2520).

---

## Pre-Flight Checklist

Before creating an issue, verify:

- [ ] **Forgejo API accessible:** `flu issue list` returns results (not errors)
- [ ] **Labels available:** `flu issue labels` shows available labels
- [ ] **Not a duplicate:** Check existing issues first
- [ ] **Check for templates:** `flu issue create --template list`
- [ ] **Identify relevant attachments:** docs/specs/logs/screenshots are collected for `flu issue attach`

```bash
# Quick connectivity check
flu issue list --limit 1

# Check for available issue templates
flu issue create --template list
```

If API fails, see **Debugging API Failures** section below.

## Check Memory for Related Work

Before creating an issue, query persistent memory for related prior work:

```
Use the mem-search skill to find:
- Similar issues that were previously filed (avoid duplicates)
- Past work on the same component or feature area
- Architectural decisions that may affect the new issue's scope
```

Reference any related findings in the issue body to provide historical context. If claude-mem is not available, skip this step and proceed to creating the issue.

---

## Creating the Issue

### Step 0: Check for Templates (Recommended)

Before creating an issue, check if the project has issue templates:

```bash
flu issue create --template list
```

**If templates are available**, use them! Templates provide:
- Consistent issue structure
- Auto-applied labels (e.g., `type:bug`, `type:enhancement`)
- Pre-filled sections to guide issue creation

**Common templates:**
- `bug-report` - Use for bugs and defects
- `feature-request` - Use for new features and enhancements

### Step 1: Create Issue with Template (Preferred)

**If a matching template exists, use it:**

```bash
# For bugs - use bug-report template
flu issue create --template bug-report --title "[BUG] Description of the bug" --body "Actual description of the bug, reproduction steps, and error messages"

# For features - use feature-request template
flu issue create --template feature-request --title "[FEATURE] Description of feature" --body "Actual description of the feature and its value"
```

**CRITICAL:** Always pass `--body` with the actual issue description. The `--template` flag provides auto-labels, but without `--body` the issue body will contain only the template boilerplate instead of a real description.

### Step 2: Create Issue Without Template (Fallback)

**If no templates exist or none match your issue type:**

```bash
# Minimal (REQUIRED) - Test this works first
flu issue create --title "Descriptive title" --body "Issue description"
```

**CRITICAL:** Never run `flu issue create` without `--title` and `--body` flags. Interactive mode does not work in Claude Code.

### Step 3: Add Labels (REQUIRED)

**CRITICAL:** Every issue MUST have labels from ALL required groups. This is not optional.

After creating the issue, immediately add labels from each required group:

```bash
# Set ALL required fields at once (recommended)
flu issue update <issue-number> --type enhancement --priority medium --state research

# Or set individually:
# Type (REQUIRED - pick one): bug, enhancement, documentation, refactor, cleanup, testing
flu issue update <issue-number> --type enhancement

# For EPICs — set state to epic (no type/priority needed)
flu issue state <issue-number> epic

# Priority (REQUIRED - pick one): critical, high, medium, low
flu issue update <issue-number> --priority medium

# State (REQUIRED - pick one based on complexity):
#   Trivial fix        -> implement
#   Simple issue       -> implement
#   Needs research     -> research
#   Incomplete/draft   -> research
flu issue state <issue-number> research
```

**Required fields (minimum 3):**
- **Type (pick one):** `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, `refactor`, `cleanup`, `testing`
- **Priority (pick one):** `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`
- **State (pick one):** `research`, `implement`

**EPICs:**
- Set state to `epic` — no type/priority needed

Use `flu issue labels` to see the full list.

### Step 4: Add Dependencies (If Applicable)

Link related issues to establish traceability:

```bash
# Reference blocking issues in the body
flu issue edit <issue-number> --body "Depends on: #123, #124"

# Or add as comment
flu issue comment <issue-number> --body "Blocked by #123"
```

**Dependency Types:**
- **Depends on** - This issue requires another to be completed first
- **Blocks** - This issue prevents another from starting
- **Related to** - Informational link to similar issues

### Step 5: Attach Relevant Documents and Evidence (REQUIRED when files exist)

**CRITICAL:** Attach all relevant supporting files available at issue creation time. Do not defer this when the files already exist.

Attach relevant artifacts such as:
- Design docs/specs (`docs/*.md`, ADRs, requirement notes)
- Error logs and command output files
- Screenshots, recordings, traces, or repro artifacts
- Config samples or fixture files that clarify reproduction

**If no relevant files exist**, explicitly state that in an issue comment so reviewers know attachment discovery was performed.

```bash
# Attach relevant files
flu issue attach <issue-number> error-log.txt screenshot.png

# If nothing relevant exists, leave explicit traceability
flu issue comment <issue-number> --body "Attachment check complete: no relevant documents/artifacts were available at issue creation time."
```

## Issue Writing Guidelines

### One Issue, One Purpose (CRITICAL)

**Each issue MUST contain exactly ONE bug fix OR ONE enhancement - never both, never multiple.**

- **ONE bug per issue** - If you find multiple bugs, create separate issues for each
- **ONE enhancement per issue** - If a feature has multiple parts, use the EPIC pattern
- **Never mix types** - Don't combine a bug fix with an enhancement in the same issue

**Why this matters:**
- Clear tracking and accountability
- Easier code review (PRs map 1:1 to issues)
- Better release notes and changelogs
- Simpler rollback if something breaks

**If you have multiple items:** Create an EPIC with child issues, or create separate standalone issues.

### Title Format
- Be specific and descriptive
- Include affected component if applicable
- Example: "Fix login timeout in auth service" (not "Fix bug")

### Body Format
Include:
1. **What:** Clear description of the issue/feature
2. **Why:** Business value or impact
3. **Context:** Related issues, error messages, or reproduction steps

---

## When to Create EPIC/Child Issues

**Use EPIC pattern when:**
- Feature has 3+ distinct implementation phases
- Multiple files/components affected
- Work spans more than one session
- Feature needs parallel workstreams

**Always err on the side of EPIC/child** - it's easier to manage smaller issues than one monolithic issue.

### Creating an EPIC

```bash
# Create parent EPIC
flu issue create --title "[EPIC] Feature description" --body "High-level description of the feature..."
flu issue state <number> epic
# Create child issues referencing EPIC
flu issue create --title "[Phase 1] First component (EPIC #<parent>)" --body "Part of EPIC #<parent>. Specific task description..."
flu issue update <number> --type enhancement --priority medium --state research```

### EPIC Title Format
- **Parent:** `[EPIC] High-level feature description`
- **Children:** `[Phase N] Specific task (EPIC #<parent-number>)`

### EPIC Body Template

For the parent EPIC issue, use this structure:

```markdown
## Summary
High-level description of the feature being implemented.

## Phases
- [ ] Phase 1: Component A (#<child-1>)
- [ ] Phase 2: Component B (#<child-2>)
- [ ] Phase 3: Testing & Documentation (#<child-3>)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All phases completed
- [ ] Tests passing
- [ ] Documentation updated
```

### Child Issue Body Template

For child issues, reference the parent:

```markdown
## Summary
Specific task description.

## Parent Issue
Part of EPIC #<parent-number>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Specific criterion 1
- [ ] Specific criterion 2
```

---

## After Creating the Issue

1. **Note the issue number** returned by the create command
2. **Attach relevant documents/evidence** using `flu issue attach` (or comment that none were available)
3. **Identify documentation updates** - see Documentation Impact section below
4. **For simple issues:** Document solution in issue comment, then run the implement skill with <number>
5. **For complex issues:** Run the research skill with <number> to analyze and design the solution
6. **When ready to implement:** Run the implement skill with <number>
7. **When complete:** Run the finish skill or the review skill with <number>

### Documentation Impact

After creating the issue, identify what documentation may need updating alongside the implementation:

**Check these documentation types:**
- [ ] `README.md` - Does this affect user-facing features or usage?
- [ ] `docs/` directory - Does this require technical documentation updates?
- [ ] CLI help text - Does this change command syntax or flags?
- [ ] `.claude/` workflows - Does this affect existing workflow templates?
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` / project instructions - Does this change project standards?
- [ ] Code docstrings - Do new public functions need documentation? (only where logic isn't self-evident)

**If documentation updates are needed**, add them to the issue body or as a comment:

```bash
flu issue comment <number> --body "## Documentation Updates Required
- [ ] docs/cli-commands.md - Document new command syntax
- [ ] README.md - Add feature to features list"
```

**Key rules:**
- Prefer editing existing docs over creating new files
- Documentation updates should be part of implementation, not a separate task

### Workflow Decision Tree

**Use the research skill if ANY of these apply:**
- Issue affects multiple files/components
- Multiple implementation approaches possible
- Unclear what code needs to change
- Need to explore codebase first
- Complex issue requiring detailed analysis

**Skip the research skill if ALL of these are true:**
- Single file change
- Obvious solution
- Simple bug fix or small enhancement
- You can provide full implementation instructions immediately

### Inline Implementation Instructions (REQUIRED when skipping R&P)

**If you are skipping the research skill, you MUST provide ALL of the following in the issue body or a comment.** This is non-negotiable - the implementer needs complete instructions to execute without making design decisions.

```bash
flu issue comment <number> --body "## Implementation Instructions

**Step 1:** [exact action - what file, what function, what change]
**Step 2:** [exact action - what file, what function, what change]
**Step 3:** [exact action - what file, what function, what change]

**Files to Modify:**
- \`path/to/file.py\` (lines X-Y) - [specific change description]

**Key Decisions (already decided - NOT for implementer):**
- Decision: [what was decided] - Rationale: [why]

**Tests to Write:**
- \`test_name\` - [what it verifies]

**Related Code Patterns:**
- \`path/to/similar.py\` line N - [what to reference]
"
```

**If you cannot provide this level of detail, you MUST use the research skill instead.** Vague issues waste implementer compute and lead to inconsistent implementations.

Then proceed to implementation.

## Debugging API Failures

If `flu issue create` fails, follow this diagnostic sequence:

### 1. Check Basic Connectivity

```bash
# Test API access
flu issue list --limit 1
```

**If this fails:**
- Check network connectivity
- Verify Forgejo token is configured: `flu config show | grep -i token`
- Token may have expired or been revoked

### 2. Test Minimal Create

```bash
# Absolute minimal test
flu issue create --title "Test issue" --body "Test"
```

**If this works:** The API is functional. Add complexity incrementally.

**If this fails:** Check the error message:
- `401 Unauthorized` - Token issue
- `422 Unprocessable Entity` - Invalid request format
- `Connection refused` - Network/server issue

### 3. Incremental Complexity

Add features one at a time to identify what fails:

```bash
# Step 1: Minimal (test first)
flu issue create --title "Title" --body "Body"

# Step 2: Add labels separately after creation
flu issue add-labels <number> type:enhancement

# Step 3: Add attachments separately
flu issue attach <number> file.txt
```

### 4. Common Failure Patterns

| Error | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `401 Unauthorized` | Invalid/expired token | Reconfigure: `flu config set forgejo_token` |
| `422 Unprocessable Entity` | Invalid field values | Use minimal create, add labels separately |
| `Connection refused` | Server unreachable | Check network, verify Forgejo URL |
| `Interactive mode` prompt | Missing required args | Always use `--title` and `--body` flags |

### 5. Token Verification

```bash
# Check current configuration
flu config show

# Test with simple API call
flu issue list --limit 1
```

## Development Standards (ENFORCED)

When implementing issues, follow fluxaos architectural standards.

**Pre-commit hooks will BLOCK commits with violations.**

### Standards Quick Reference

| # | Standard | Requirement |
|---|----------|-------------|
| 1 | No Hardcoded Variables | All paths, URLs, file lists from config |
| 2 | No Fallbacks | Fail fast with clear errors |
| 3 | Config-Driven/Modular | Everything configurable |
| 4 | Dynamic Paths | Use path helpers only |
| 5 | DRY Principles | Use existing helpers (see `docs/python-functions-reference.md`) |
| 6 | Consistent CLI Output | Use print_* helpers |
| 7 | File Size Limit | Max ~500 lines per file |

See `.claude/ARCHITECTURAL_STANDARDS.md` for complete details.

For workflow details, see `.claude/WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md` - Workflow 1.

---

## Testing Requirements - ZERO EXCEPTIONS

ALL 3 test types are **MANDATORY**. There are **NO EXCEPTIONS**. Ever.

| # | Tool | What | Required |
|---|------|------|----------|
| 1 | **ruff** | Lint/syntax | ALWAYS - NO EXCEPTIONS |
| 2 | **pytest** | Real command execution | ALWAYS - NO EXCEPTIONS |
| 3 | **Playwright** | Real browser testing | ALWAYS for webapp - NO EXCEPTIONS |

### What is BANNED
- `unittest.mock`, `@patch`, `MagicMock`, `Mock()`, `mocker.patch`
- `pytest-mock` library
- Any pattern that replaces real behavior with fake behavior
- Pre-commit hook BLOCKS commits with mock patterns

**"Skipping" tests is not acceptable. Ever.**
**"NOT_APPLICABLE" is not a valid justification for webapp projects.**
